_doc.what: Hand-authored map: our pool slug -> the source movement whose illustration we ship.
_doc.why_hand_mapped: Names do not line up mechanically ('Barbell Bench Press' vs 'bench-press', 'Pec Deck Fly' vs 'butterfly-machine'), and a wrong illustration is worse than none — it teaches the wrong movement. Anything not listed here simply ships without an image.
_doc.pipeline: scripts/import_pool_images.py downloads, trims, resizes and converts to webp under web/public/exercises/<slug>-N.webp. We host our own copies; nothing is hotlinked. CC BY-SA requires attribution wherever the image is shown and keeps our processed copies under the same licence.
_doc.frames: Two per movement: start and end position.
_doc.removed_2026_08_09: A multi-persona review viewed all 96 illustrations against their captions; these 12 showed a different movement and were dropped rather than remapped, because the source has no correct frame for them: t_bar_row (shows a stability-ball plank/knee-tuck); smith_incline_press (byte-identical to t_bar_row; same stability-ball plank); plank (shows a rounded-back quadruped knee-tuck, not a plank); bb_overhead_press (drawn seated; this entry is the standing press); cable_external_rotation (shows a straight-arm horizontal pull-in, not a rotation); hack_squat (both frames are the same file, so no range of motion is shown); ab_wheel_rollout (shows a barbell rollout; the entry (and its Russian name) is the wheel); arnold_press (plain dumbbell press without the rotation that defines the Arnold); bent_over_db_reverse_fly (drawn prone on a bench; this entry is the standing hinge version); reverse_lunge (same drawing as walking_lunge; shows neither direction of travel); band_pull_apart (band runs to an external anchor; a pull-apart is held at both ends)
_doc.upstream_defects: The source repository itself ships wrong files for some movements, verified by hash: t-bar-rows-1.png and smith-machine-incline-bench-press-1.png are byte-identical upstream (both a stability-ball plank), and hack-squat-machine-1/2 are one file, so those entries have no recoverable illustration at all. `duplicate_image_errors` in the build script exists because of this.

sources.everkinetic-repo: github.com/everkinetic/data — CC BY-SA 4.0. A bare string value uses this.
sources.commons: commons.wikimedia.org — the same artist, uploaded per file and CC BY-SA 3.0 there. Used where the repo's file is wrong: it serves byte-identical images for t-bar-rows and smith-machine-incline-bench-press, and one file for both frames of hack-squat-machine. Value is {"source": "commons", "files": [...]}.
sources.wger: wger.de — community-contributed, so it covers movements Everkinetic has no vocabulary for (face pull, kettlebell swing, chest-supported row) but mixes several visual styles. Only two families are taken: the grey anatomical render with a red highlight, and plain line art. Photographs, dark-background renders and flat cartoons are refused, as is any drawing showing different equipment than the entry names. Each image carries its own author and licence, because CC BY-SA credits a person, not a site. Value is {"source": "wger", "urls": [...], "author": "...", "license": "...", "style": "photo"}.
